control_arm.trace_note: Subsampled every 8th point of a 4001-point grid for file size.

model.name: SHH-GREM1-BMP-FGF limb bud outgrowth loop (caricature)

variables.name: former-ZPA descendant zone
variables.units: fraction of Grem1-competent mesenchyme displaced, in [0,1]

edges.claim: AER FGF4 signalling maintains the polarizing region (SHH/FGF4 feedback loop).
SHH signalling is required for maintenance of Gremlin.
BMP4 first initiates Grem1; SHH then propagates it (differential transcriptional regulation of Grem1).
The secreted BMP antagonist Gremlin relays the SHH signal by antagonising BMP.
Gremlin-mediated BMP antagonism is what induces Fgf4 in the AER; BMP therefore represses AER Fgf and GREM1 de-represses it.
FGF signalling can repress Grem1 expression (a novel Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop); the repression is dependent on high FGF activity.
Shh-expressing cells and their descendants cannot express Gremlin; their proliferation forms a barrier separating the Shh signal from Gremlin-expressing cells, which breaks down the Shh-Fgf4 loop.
The expanding former-ZPA descendant zone is refractory to Grem1 expression, so it removes Grem1-competent mesenchyme.
Readout edge. In Fgf10-null mice limb bud formation initiates but outgrowth does not occur and the AER does not form, so AER FGF is taken as the proximate driver of progenitor expansion.

parameters.name: d_S
parameters.source: Defines the time unit: time is measured in SHH turnover times.
parameters.note: Not a free parameter; it sets the clock.

parameters.name: K_FS
parameters.note: AER FGF level at which ZPA Shh maintenance is half-maximal. No measured dose-response for AER-FGF -> Shh exists; set below the operating FGF level so the wild-type loop is maintained, not marginal.

parameters.name: n_FS
parameters.note: Cooperativity of FGF -> Shh. >1 so the loop has a defined engage point rather than a graded ramp; 3 is the smallest value giving a clean ignition threshold.

parameters.name: a_B
parameters.note: Weight of the BMP -> Grem1 INITIATION arm (Benazet 2009). Deliberately set below the value at which this arm alone sustains the loop, so that it produces a transient that SHH must catch. With a_B large enough to self-sustain, an Shh-null limb overgrows, which is wrong.

parameters.name: K_BG
parameters.note: Half-maximal BMP for Grem1 induction.

parameters.name: n_BG
parameters.note: Cooperativity of BMP -> Grem1.

parameters.name: a_S
parameters.note: Weight of the SHH -> Grem1 PROPAGATION arm (Zuniga 1999, Benazet 2009). Larger than a_B because SHH, not BMP, is what maintains Grem1.

parameters.name: K_SG
parameters.note: Half-maximal SHH for Grem1 maintenance.

parameters.name: n_SG
parameters.note: Cooperativity of SHH -> Grem1.

parameters.name: K_FG
parameters.note: FGF level at which Grem1 repression is half-maximal. Set ABOVE the loop's operating FGF level because Verheyden & Sun 2008 report the repression is 'dependent on high FGF activity' -- it must not engage until the loop has run.

parameters.name: n_FG
parameters.note: Cooperativity of the FGF -| Grem1 repression.

parameters.name: d_G
parameters.note: GREM1 turnover, faster than SHH: Benazet 2009 place BMP/GREM1 in the FAST module and SHH/GREM1/FGF in the SLOW loop.

parameters.name: b_prod
parameters.note: Chosen with d_B so the unantagonised BMP steady state is exactly 1.0.

parameters.name: d_B
parameters.note: BMP turnover, 10x SHH: the fast module of Benazet 2009.

parameters.name: k_seq
parameters.note: Rate at which GREM1 removes active BMP (Zuniga 1999: GREM1 is a secreted BMP antagonist). Must exceed d_B for antagonism to move BMP at all; at k_seq < d_B the loop cannot engage for any knob setting.

parameters.name: K_BF
parameters.note: BMP level at which AER Fgf repression is half-maximal.

parameters.name: n_BF
parameters.note: Cooperativity of BMP -| Fgf.

parameters.name: d_F
parameters.note: AER FGF turnover, same order as SHH (the slow loop).

parameters.name: k_Z
parameters.note: Rate at which former-ZPA descendants expand and displace Grem1-competent mesenchyme (Scherz 2004). Sets the LENGTH of the outgrowth window; it is the single parameter the window duration is most sensitive to.

parameters.name: K_SZ
parameters.note: SHH level above which cells are counted as former-ZPA.

parameters.name: n_SZ
parameters.note: Cooperativity of the descendant-zone source term.

parameters.name: K_FL
parameters.note: AER FGF level needed to drive distal progenitor expansion. A READOUT definition, not a regulatory edge.

parameters.name: n_FL
parameters.note: Sharpness of the outgrowth readout. Set high deliberately: at n=6 the sub-threshold FGF leak integrates, over the 80-time-unit window, into a spurious 3%-of-wild-type 'rudiment' in arms where the loop never engages. That number was an artifact of the readout, not a result.

model.nondimensionalisation: Time is measured in SHH turnover times (d_S = 1 by definition). Each species is scaled by its own maximum, so the unantagonised BMP steady state and the underepressed AER FGF steady state are both 1.0 at wild-type settings. This removes 2 parameters (d_S is fixed to 1 by the time unit; b_prod is fixed by d_B so that maximal BMP is 1) and makes every Hill constant readable as a fraction of maximum. 21 of the 23 parameters remain free, and all 21 are labelled assumed; none is labelled sourced.

s.label: ZPA Shh transcriptional output  s
s.meaning: Fraction of wild-type ZPA Shh output. This is what a ZRS allele changes.
s.claim: Genomic substitution of the mouse ZRS with snake orthologs caused severe limb reduction; restoring a single lost transcription factor binding site reinstated full in vivo function.
s.also_claim: In python hindlimb buds SHH transcription is weak and transient, leading to early termination of the genetic circuit that drives limb outgrowth.

phi.label: AER initiation / FGF10 input  phi
phi.meaning: Strength of the AER-initiating input (FGF10 -> FGF8 AER induction). phi = 0 is the Fgf10-null route.
phi.claim: Fgf10-/- mice show complete truncation of fore- and hindlimbs; limb bud formation initiates but outgrowth does not occur, and neither AER nor ZPA forms.
phi.also_claim: Human WNT3 Q83X causes tetra-amelia, placing an upstream initiation failure on the same route to complete limb absence.

g.label: GREM1 production  g
g.meaning: Scale on both Grem1 induction arms. g = 0 is the Grem1-null route.
g.claim: In early limb buds mesenchymal Grem1 is required to establish a functional AER and the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback signalling that propagates SHH; the core mesenchymal cells of the limb bud are eliminated by apoptosis.

bmp.label: BMP production  b
bmp.meaning: Scale on BMP production. BMP both initiates Grem1 and represses AER Fgf, so it is required at both ends of the loop.
bmp.claim: BMP4 first initiates and SHH then propagates e-m feedback signalling through differential transcriptional regulation of Grem1.

F_on.note: AER FGF level defining 'the loop is engaged'.

T_end.note: Simulated window in SHH turnover times.

readout_definitions.outgrowth: L(T_end), the time integral of a sharp Hill function of AER FGF; a proxy for proximodistal extent, reported only as a fraction of the wild-type control because the model has no absolute length scale.

model.initial_condition: S=G=F=Z=L=0; B at its unantagonised steady state b*b_prod/d_B. BMP is present first because Benazet 2009 report BMP4 initiates Grem1.

s.label: ZPA Shh transcriptional output  s
s.meaning: Fraction of wild-type ZPA Shh output. This is what a ZRS allele changes.
s.claim: Genomic substitution of the mouse ZRS with snake orthologs caused severe limb reduction; restoring a single lost transcription factor binding site reinstated full in vivo function.
s.also_claim: In python hindlimb buds SHH transcription is weak and transient, leading to early termination of the genetic circuit that drives limb outgrowth.
s.threshold_definition: Value of the knob at which AER FGF first exceeds F_on = 0.35 at some time, i.e. the ignition bifurcation of the loop. Located by 45-step bisection.
s.threshold_uncertainty_basis: Full spread of the bisected threshold across 4 integrator/tolerance settings, floored at 0.0001 (below which the number is not meaningful for an uncalibrated model).

arms.arm: no FGF-|Grem1 repression (K_FG -> inf; Verheyden & Sun 2008 removed)

termination_ablation.finding: In this parameterisation the Scherz 2004 descendant-zone ratchet is what terminates the loop: removing it, the loop never switches off within 200 time units. Removing the Verheyden & Sun 2008 FGF-|Grem1 repression instead leaves termination intact and lengthens the window by +4.0%. The two published mechanisms are therefore NOT equal partners here, and the model leans almost entirely on one of them.
termination_ablation.caveat: This is a property of this parameter set, not a claim about which mechanism dominates in a limb bud. No parameter scan was run, and k_Z is assumed.

null_control.name: null (all production zero, zero initial condition)
null_control.expectation: all 6 states identically zero for all t

positive_control_of_classifier.case: no BMP (b=0): nothing to terminate the loop

outgrowth_consistency.name: outgrowth: ODE state vs trapezoid re-integration

deterministic.name: no RNG in the model
deterministic.expectation: model uses no random numbers; the run is reproducible without a seed

derived_counts.name: derived counts match the data they describe
derived_counts.expectation: no prose count disagrees with the table it describes

phenotype_classes.no-limb: The loop never engages (AER FGF never exceeds F_on = 0.35) and accumulated outgrowth is below 5% of the wild-type control. In the model this means 'this feedback loop contributed no outgrowth'. It does NOT mean amelia in an embryo: the model contains no SHH-independent proximal outgrowth, so it cannot distinguish a Shh-null limb (which in mice still forms a stylopod) from true limb absence.
phenotype_classes.truncated: The loop engages and self-terminates, but accumulated outgrowth is between 5% and 85% of the wild-type control.
phenotype_classes.normal: The loop engages, self-terminates, and accumulated outgrowth is within 85%-115% of the wild-type control.
phenotype_classes.overgrowth: The loop engages and self-terminates, but accumulated outgrowth exceeds 115% of the wild-type control.
phenotype_classes.fails-to-terminate: AER FGF is still above F_on at the end of the simulated window (t = 80 SHH turnover times). The loop has no off switch in this parameter regime.

limitations: This is a SIMULATION. No quantity in this file is an observation of any embryo.

The model is a caricature of a signalling TOPOLOGY. It is not calibrated to any measured mouse limb bud: no concentration, rate, diffusion length or developmental time in it was fitted to data, and none should be read as one.

21 of the 23 parameters are assumed and none is sourced; the other 2 are fixed by the non-dimensionalisation. They were chosen so the wild-type arm initiates, is maintained and self-terminates -- that is, the control arm's qualitative behaviour was an input to parameter choice, not an independent result.
A threshold in this model is a threshold in this model. It is not a prediction of the ZRS allelic series at which a mouse loses a limb, and it has no units that could be compared to one.

The model is non-spatial: SHH, GREM1, BMP and FGF are single well-mixed levels. The real loop is spatially organised across an epithelial-mesenchymal boundary with measured gradients, and the Scherz 2004 mechanism it borrows is explicitly geometric (an expanding descendant zone). Variable Z is a zero-dimensional stand-in for that geometry.

The model contains no SHH-independent proximal outgrowth, so it cannot distinguish a Shh-null limb -- which in mice still forms proximal skeleton -- from true amelia. Its 'no-limb' class means only 'this loop never engaged'.

Digit number and digit pattern are outside the model. Sheth et al. 2012 (PMID 23239739) show digit patterning is a Turing-type mechanism whose wavelength distal Hox genes set; none of that is represented here, so the model says nothing about how many digits form.
The knob s is held constant in time. In python hindlimb buds the reported defect is that SHH is weak AND transient (PMID 27773569); a time-varying s is not explored.
Only the classifier's boundaries, not the model, decide where 'truncated' ends and 'normal' begins. Those cuts (5%, 85%, 115% of the wild-type control) are assumed.
The outgrowth window duration is most sensitive to k_Z, a wholly assumed parameter. No sensitivity analysis over the full parameter space was run.

The two published termination mechanisms are not equal partners in this parameterisation. The ablation arm shows the loop leans almost entirely on the Scherz 2004 descendant-zone ratchet: without it the loop never terminates, while without the Verheyden & Sun 2008 FGF-|Grem1 repression it still terminates, about 4% later. So the self-terminating behaviour shown in the control figure is mostly one mechanism, and which mechanism dominates in a real limb bud is not addressed here.
